title: Room call button opens the start-call popup with the device controls
description: With the call window off the room popup is still the only place mic and camera are chosen, so it must keep both controls and must not open any window on the click.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = Off (the default). Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A direct message between user1 and user2 exists and both have it open.
postconditions: Nothing to restore: the settings are at their defaults. Close any call window still open.
steps_actions:
1. As user1, open the direct message with user2 and click the camera (Video call) button in the room header.
2. Toggle the camera control on and the microphone control off.
3. Press Escape.
steps_result:
1. A "Start a call" popup opens over the room, naming user2. It carries a camera toggle and a microphone toggle in its header and a "Start call" button. No new browser window or tab has opened.
2. Both controls change state in place; the popup stays open and nothing is sent yet.
3. The popup closes. No conference message was posted in the room and no call appears in the room's call history (kebab > Video conferences).

title: A direct call rings from the room: caller waits, callee is popped

preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = Off (the default). Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A direct message between user1 and user2 exists and both have it open.
postconditions: Nothing to restore: the settings are at their defaults. Close any call window still open.
steps_actions:
1. As user1, click the room header camera button and confirm with "Start call".

steps_result:

2. An "Incoming call from" popup covers user2's screen naming user1, with Accept, Decline and a "Mute and dismiss" cross. A ring tone plays.
3. Both popups close. A new browser tab opens for user1 and for user2 at the provider's own page (a jitsi URL, not a /conference/ URL on the workspace).
4. A video-conference message block is present, naming the call and offering "Join call".

Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. 3. Still no navbar video button and still no request to video-conference.joinable. The ring is announced by the incoming popup and the sidebar group only.

title: The call ends about ten seconds after the last person leaves
description: Ending is a consequence of the call being empty, and the grace period is what makes a reload survivable.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As the only participant, close the call window and immediately start a stopwatch.
2. Watch the conference message block in #qa-calls in the main app.
3. Open the navbar video dropdown.
4. Check the room's call history (kebab > Video conferences).
steps_result:
1. The call window closes and the main app comes to the foreground.
2. For about ten seconds it still offers "Join call". After the grace period it stops offering to join and reads as an ended call.
3. The call is no longer listed (and the button is gone if nothing else is running).
4. The call is listed as ended, with a duration consistent with how long the window was open.
suite: Flag ON - leaving and ending a call

title: Reloading the call window does not end the call

steps_actions:

3. Check the navbar video dropdown from a second user's session.
steps_result:

steps_actions:

2. Start a conference in #qa-calls and open the chat panel in the call window.
3. Post a message in the panel and look at #qa-calls in the main app.
4. Check #qa-calls for a new discussion, and the conference record for a discussionRid.

steps_actions:

2. Post "hello from the call" in the panel and look at #qa-calls in the main app.
3. Have user2 join the call, then check user2's thread following state on the conference message in the main app (kebab on the message > Following).
4. Have user1 post another thread reply.
5. Have user2 leave and rejoin the call.
steps_result:
1. The panel header reads "Thread in # qa-calls" and shows a thread message list scoped to the conference message, with a composer.
2. The message appears as a reply in the thread under the conference message, not as a channel message. No discussion room was created off #qa-calls.
3. user2 is following the thread without having asked to - joining the call auto-followed them.

5. They are still following the thread exactly once - no duplicate subscription.

title: A workspace already running persistent chat sees no change until it opts in
description: The one thing this feature must not do is change what workspaces already running persistent chat see. With the window off, the server answers main_room whatever the mode setting was left at.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = Off (the default). Settings: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = On, Discussion_enabled = On. The active provider app declares the persistentChat capability (the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 does NOT - see the README). Verify with GET /api/v1/video-conference.capabilities before starting. A public channel #qa-calls with user1 and user2.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled to Off and VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat back to its original value.
steps_actions:
1. As an admin, look at VideoConf_Persistent_Chat_Mode in Admin > Settings > Video Conference.
2. Start a conference in #qa-calls from the room popup as user1.
3. Turn VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled On, set the mode to thread, then turn the window back Off and start another conference.
steps_result:
1. It is disabled: it needs the conference window on as well, so a workspace with the window off cannot even set it.
2. The provider's page opens in a new tab, exactly as before, and a discussion is created off #qa-calls - the main_room behaviour persistent chat has always had.
3. A discussion is created again, not a thread: with the window off the server falls back to main_room whatever the mode is left at, so turning the window off puts the workspace back exactly where it was.

title: A URL provider runs the whole flow inside the call window
description: A provider reached by URL is the only kind of provider reachable on this branch. Its page is embedded in an iframe, so it must be allowed to be framed and it gets the permissions the call needs.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. The active provider is a self-hosted Jitsi (not the public meet.jit.si, which disconnects embedded calls after five minutes) or Google Meet. A direct message between user1 and user2.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user1, place a direct call to user2 and enter it.
2. Check the frame in devtools > Elements.
3. Check the URL the frame was given.
4. Have user2 answer and confirm the join.
steps_result:
1. The call window shows the provider's own call UI inside the window, with working audio/video controls of the provider's own.
2. The provider page is in an iframe whose allow attribute grants camera, microphone, display-capture, fullscreen, autoplay and speaker-selection, with referrerPolicy strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
3. It carries a name query parameter with user1's display name, so they arrive named rather than anonymous.
4. Both are in the same provider room and can see and hear each other.

title: A provider page that refuses framing leaves the call area blank

preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. The active provider is configured with a URL that sends a restrictive X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors header (for example a provider instance behind a proxy that sets X-Frame-Options: DENY). A direct message between user1 and user2.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user1, place a direct call to user2 and enter it.
2. Look at the call area and the browser console.
3. Close the window.
steps_result:
1. The call window opens with our top bar, timer and panel buttons all present and working.
2. The call area is blank and the console carries a framing refusal from the browser. Nothing about the workspace is broken: the panels, the members list and the chat still work.
3. The leave is reported and the call ends normally after the grace period.

title: A conference member with no access to the call's room reaches their own call
description: This is the whole point of the membership model: a users[] entry authorises joining the call without granting any room access. The third person in a DM call is the case it exists for.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A direct message between user1 and user2. user3 has no access to it. user1 has placed a direct call to user2 and both are in it.

steps_actions:
1. As user1, add user3 to the conference from the People panel.
2. As user3, join the call from the navbar dropdown and confirm "Join call".
3. As user3, check the sidebar and try to open the DM.
4. As user3, open the chat panel in the call window.
5. As user3, open the People panel.
steps_result:
1. user3 is rung and appears in the People panel.
2. user3 enters the call successfully - no room membership was needed and none was granted.
3. The DM is not in user3's sidebar and is not reachable.
4. It shows "Chat not shared with you" with an explanation, rather than a missing-page or permission error.
5. user3 sees themselves in "In call" with a balloon-off icon beside their name titled "No chat access". The Add people button is not offered to them.

title: A stranger gets nothing useful from a conference id
description: Every endpoint authorises through one check and answers both failures the same vague way, so a call id cannot be used to learn that a call is real.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A private group qa-private with user1 and user2 only. user1 has a conference running in it. user3 is not a member of the group and not a member of the conference. You have the conference's callId.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user3, open /conference/<callId> in a browser window.
2. As user3, call GET /api/v1/video-conference.info?callId=<callId>.
3. As user3, call GET /api/v1/video-conference.info with a callId made up at random.
4. As user3, call POST /api/v1/video-conference.join with the real callId.
steps_result:
1. A "Call not found" state page is shown - not a preflight, not a members list, and nothing that confirms the call exists.
2. The response is a failure reading invalid-params - the same answer a callId that does not exist at all would give.
3. The same invalid-params failure, indistinguishable from the previous step.
4. It fails with invalid-params; user3 does not appear in the conference's users list.

A third browser profile is signed in as user3, who has no access.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. Open /conference/<callId> in a private window with nobody signed in.
2. Sign in as user3 in that window.
3. Click Logout.
4. Sign in as user2 in the same window.
steps_result:
1. The login form is shown (the conference is not served to a guest). It does not flash and then disappear.
2. The window stays on /conference/<callId> and shows a "You are not authorized to view this page" state, saying which account is signed in, with a Logout action.
3. The window logs out but stays on the /conference/<callId> URL rather than navigating to the workspace home.
4. The window lands back on the same conference, on its join preflight - not on /home.

title: Ringing needs the videoconf-ring-users permission; everything else does not
description: Having access to a conference must not be a way around the permission that gates ringing. Starting a call and adding people still work, they just do not ring.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. Admin > Permissions: videoconf-ring-users has been removed from the user role. user1 and user2 both hold only the user role. A direct message between user1 and user2, and a public channel #qa-calls with user1, user2 and user3.
postconditions: Restore the videoconf-ring-users permission on the user role and set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off.
steps_actions:
1. As user1, place a direct call to user2 and enter it.
2. As user2, open the navbar video dropdown.
3. As user1, open the People panel and click the phone (ring) button on user2's row.
4. As user1, add user3 to the conference with "Ring people" checked.
5. Restore videoconf-ring-users on the user role and ring user2 again.
steps_result:
1. user1 lands in the call and the conference message is posted, but user2 hears no ring and gets no notification - the ring degrades silently.
2. The call is listed as a running call and can be joined - the list is the route in.
3. The ring is refused with an error toast, and POST /api/v1/video-conference.ring answers 403 "Not allowed".
4. user3 is added successfully (a success toast, and they appear in the panel) but is not rung.
5. The ring goes out: user2 hears the tone and their navbar button turns red.

title: A script URL handed to the conference route opens nothing
description: The provider URL is opened in a window of ours. A javascript: or data: "URL" is not somewhere to go but something to run, and it would run in whatever window was opened for it - which, until it navigates, is our own blank one. So only an absolute http(s) address is accepted.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. Signed in as user1. Browser popups allowed for the workspace origin.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. Navigate the main app window to /conference/x?callUrl=javascript:alert(document.domain)%26
2. Repeat with /conference/x?callUrl=data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>%26
3. Repeat with /conference/x?callUrl=/admin/settings%26 (a relative address).
4. Check the browser console.
steps_result:
1. No new window or tab opens, no alert fires, and no "popup blocked" modal appears - claiming the popup was blocked would be a lie with advice attached.
2. Again nothing opens and no script runs.
3. Nothing opens. In particular no window opens showing the workspace at /admin/settings - a relative address has no origin of its own and must not be read as an in-product conference.
4. No uncaught error; the app stays usable.

title: An external provider window keeps no handle on the workspace
description: A provider page has no business reaching back into the workspace: with a live window.opener it could navigate the tab the user came from to a page of its choosing, and a login screen is the obvious one to imitate.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. Signed in as user1. Browser popups allowed. Devtools available in the opened window.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. Navigate the main app window to /conference/x?callUrl=https://example.com%26
2. In the opened window's console, evaluate window.opener.
3. In the same console, evaluate window.name.
4. Open a second external call the same way.
steps_result:
1. A separate window opens at example.com and the main window returns to /home.
2. It is null - the window was cut loose before being sent to the provider.
3. It is empty: an external provider window is unnamed, so each external call gets a window of its own rather than sharing ours.
4. A second, separate window opens rather than the first one being navigated.

title: A conference whose record carries no usable URL does not open a window
description: A call arriving with an empty or non-web address is nothing openable. Saying the popup was blocked would be misleading, because allowing popups cannot make it succeed.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. Direct database access to the videoconference collection (a development workspace). A direct message between user1 and user2, and a conference in it that user1 can join.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. Start a conference and note its callId, then in Mongo set that conference's url field to the empty string.
2. As user1, open the call window for that conference and confirm the join.
3. Click Close.
4. Set the url to a relative value such as /room/42 and repeat.
steps_result:
1. The update reports one document modified, and re-reading the record shows url as the empty string.
2. The window shows a warning state page with the unexpected-error title and a single Close button, rather than a blank frame or a broken page.
3. The window reports leaving and closes.
4. The frame is not pointed at the workspace: nothing navigates the call window to a workspace route, and the user is not shown the app inside the call area.

title: A blocked popup asks the user to allow it, and the retry works
description: The window is opened on the click that asked for it precisely so browsers do not refuse it - but a blocker or an extension can still refuse both the popout and the plain tab, and then the user has to be asked to click again.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. Browser popups BLOCKED for the workspace origin (Chrome: site settings > Pop-ups and redirects > Block). A direct message between user1 and user2.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user1, click the room header camera button.
2. Allow popups for the site in the browser's own prompt or site settings, then use the modal's confirm action.
3. Repeat the block, then join a running call from the navbar dropdown instead.
steps_result:
1. No call window opens. A modal appears asking the user to allow the popup, with a way to try again.
2. The call window opens on the preflight for the same call.
3. The same modal appears. Note that the join has already been posted for this path, so if the user never allows the popup they are counted as joined with no window - the known gap the next join or the expiry cron closes.

title: Real audio: the ring, the dial tone and silencing them
description: Sound is the one part of this feature nothing automated can check. The ring still sounds even though the popup is gone, and the caller's dial tone has to stop when the other side answers.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A direct message between user1 and user2 exists.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. With sound on in both browsers, have user1 place a direct call to user2 and enter the call.
2. As user2, click Silence on the ringing row.
3. Wait for the 15-second ring window to lapse.
4. As user1, ring user2 again from the People panel and have user2 join.
steps_result:
1. user2 hears a repeating ring tone. user1, in the call window, hears a dial tone while user2 is still ringing.
2. user2's ring tone stops at once. user1's dial tone keeps playing - silencing told nobody anything.
3. user1's dial tone stops on its own when user2 stops reading as ringing.
4. The ring tone plays again for user2 and stops on joining; user1's dial tone stops as soon as user2 is in the call.

title: Losing access to the chat's room mid-call
description: The chat panel decides between the room and the not-shared explanation from a descriptor that is only as fresh as the last read, so a member removed during a call gets a not-found fallback until it is read again. Rare and self-correcting, but worth recognising.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A private group qa-private with user1 (owner) and user2. user1 has started a conference in it and both are in the call with the chat panel open.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user1, in the main app, remove user2 from qa-private while user2 stays in the call with the chat panel open.
2. Look at user2's chat panel.
3. Have anything move on the conference (someone joins, leaves, or is added) so the conference is read again.
4. Check that the call itself was unaffected throughout.
steps_result:
1. user2 is removed from the room.
2. It shows a not-found fallback rather than an explanation - the descriptor it decided from is stale.
3. user2's panel settles on the "Chat not shared with you" explanation, and user1 gets the chat-access banner offering to fix it.
4. user2 stayed in the call the whole time - room membership is not what authorises being there.

title: Two windows for the same call, and the call surviving the app
description: The call window is shared and is meant to outlive the main app, which is hard to assert anywhere but by hand.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. A public channel #qa-calls with user1 and user2. user2 has a conference running in it.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user1, join the conference so a call window is open, then paste the same /conference/<callId> URL into a brand-new browser window opened by hand.
2. Close one of the two windows and watch the other.
3. Close the main app window entirely, leaving the call window open.
4. Reopen the app and check the call.
steps_result:
1. The hand-opened window loads the conference independently (it is not the named shared window). user1 is in the call in both - and the same person is counted once in the members list.
2. The remaining window keeps the call. Note that closing one reports a leave, so user1 may briefly drop out of the members list until the other window's next heartbeat.
3. The call keeps running and the call window is unaffected - the watch on it is dropped rather than fired, because the main app going away is not the call window closing.
4. The call is still listed and user1 is still counted as being in it.

title: A killed call window with a URL provider stays listed until the expiry cron
description: Presence leases are swept only for a provider that runs the call in our window and reports its own room. For a URL provider the sweep deliberately stays away, so a crashed tab leaves a ghost until the 24-hour expiry - a known limitation worth confirming rather than filing as a bug.
preconditions: Workspace on an Enterprise licence that includes the videoconference-enterprise module. A video conference provider app is installed, enabled and selected as the active provider - the bundled Jitsi app v2.1.1 unless the case says otherwise - and Admin > Settings > Video Conference reports no provider problem. VideoConf_Enable_DMs, VideoConf_Enable_Channels, VideoConf_Enable_Groups and VideoConf_Enable_Teams are all On. Users user1, user2 and user3 exist with the default user role, which carries the videoconf-ring-users permission. Browser popups are allowed for the workspace origin. Unless stated otherwise you are signed in as user1 in one browser profile and as user2 in a second one, both looking at the app. Setting: Admin > Settings > Video Conference > VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled = On. Setting: VideoConf_Enable_Persistent_Chat = Off. The active provider is the bundled Jitsi app (no embedded capability). A public channel #qa-calls with user1 and user2. Both are in a conference. Ability to kill the browser process holding user2's call window.
postconditions: Set VideoConf_Conference_Window_Enabled back to Off. Close every call window still open and let any call left running end (10s after the last participant leaves).
steps_actions:
1. As user2, confirm the call window is sending heartbeats (devtools > Network, filter "heartbeat").
2. Kill user2's browser process outright (not a graceful close), so no leave is reported.
3. As user1, watch the People panel for five minutes.
4. Have user2 rejoin the call from a fresh browser.
steps_result:
1. A POST to /api/v1/video-conference.heartbeat goes out roughly every 30 seconds.
2. The window is gone and no video-conference.leave request was made.
3. user2 is still listed under "In call": the presence sweep skips calls held by a non-embedded provider, so nothing evicts them. This is expected on this branch.
4. They are counted once, in the call - the join reconciles their membership.
